newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end sharply higher on spillover.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end sharply higher on spillover.

text.p: Near-limit gains in CBOT soybean futures pushed soy product futures to sharply higher closes on Monday.
"This market is all about weather right now," said one soyoil trader. "Nothing else matters."
CBOT soybeans posted sharp gains on concerns that a spell of dry and hot weather in the central Midwest might impair the devlopment of the soybean crop, traders and analysts said.
More gains in soymeal and soyoil can be expected if the weather remains hot and dry as forecast for the balance of the week, traders said.
During the session, August soyoil rallied the 1.00 cent a lb daily limit and August soymeal jumped up the $10.00 per ton daily limit.

The rally in CBOT soymeal prices kept buyers out of U.S. cash markets Monday, but basis values were supported by crushing plants taking downtime and talk of impending export business, cash traders said.
August soymeal ended up $9.30 per ton at $254.90 and other months were $7.10 to $10.50 higher. August soyoil settled up 0.50 cent per lb at 22.43 cents, with other months 0.40 to 0.61 higher.
On the day in soymeal trade, Merrill Lynch sold 300 lots December and Refco sold 300 lots December. ING bought 200 lots December, pit traders said.
In soyoil, Cargill sold 400 lots August, 100 lots September and 500 lots December. Produce Grain sold 400 lots August and FIMAT Futures Inc. sold 400 lots August.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 21,000 lots, compared with Friday's actual volume of 20,938 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 18,000 lots, against Friday's 15,101.
